meta.titre: Moving Across Membranes: diffusion, osmosis and active transport compared
meta.sous_theme: Passive and active movement of substances into and out of cells

sections.contenu_markdown:
A woman roasts fish by the roadside in Douala, and passers-by smell it from far away. Sprinkle sugar on sliced pawpaw and a pool of liquid soon collects in the bowl. A farmer pours too much fertiliser around his maize and the leaves droop within days.
Each of these everyday events is a way in which substances move into, out of and between cells. The GCE examiners come back to diffusion, osmosis and active transport almost every year, usually asking you to define them or to compare them.

items: Particles of gases and liquids are always moving randomly.
A cell is surrounded by a cell membrane that controls what enters and leaves it.
Plant cells have a cell wall and a large vacuole filled with cell sap.
Respiration in cells releases the energy that living things use.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Definitions
- **Diffusion** is the net movement of molecules or ions from a region where they are in high concentration to a region where they are in low concentration, down a concentration gradient, as a result of their random movement. It needs no energy from the cell.
- **Osmosis** is the movement of water molecules from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution through a selectively permeable membrane. It is a special case of diffusion and only water is involved. It needs no energy from the cell.
- **Active transport** is the movement of molecules or ions across a cell membrane from a region of low concentration to a region of high concentration, that is against the concentration gradient. It needs energy released by respiration, and carrier proteins in the membrane.

### Side-by-side comparison
| Feature | Diffusion | Osmosis | Active transport |
|---|---|---|---|
| Direction | High to low concentration | Dilute to concentrated solution | Low to high concentration |
| Energy from respiration | Not needed | Not needed | Needed |
| Substance moved | Gases, small dissolved molecules | Water only | Ions and some molecules |
| Example | Oxygen moving from the air sacs of the lungs into the blood | Water entering a root hair cell from the soil | Mineral ions entering root hair cells |

### What makes diffusion faster?
A steeper concentration gradient, a higher temperature, a larger surface area and a shorter distance all make diffusion faster.

### Osmosis in cells
A plant cell in water or a very dilute solution takes in water, its vacuole swells and the cell becomes **turgid**, pressing against the cell wall. Turgid cells support leaves and young stems. In a concentrated solution a plant cell loses water, the cytoplasm shrinks away from the cell wall and the cell is said to be **plasmolysed**; a plant whose cells have lost turgor wilts. An animal cell has no cell wall, so in pure water it may burst, and in a concentrated solution it shrinks.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a practical question gives masses or lengths of tissue before and after soaking
variantes.contenu_markdown:
Cut identical cylinders from a yam, a potato or a carrot, dry them and find the mass of each. Place each in a different solution (distilled water and sugar solutions of increasing concentration) for the same time at the same temperature. Remove them, blot them dry and weigh them again.

Percentage change in mass $= \dfrac{\text{final mass} - \text{initial mass}}{\text{initial mass}} \times 100$.

A gain in mass means water entered, so the solution was more dilute than the cell sap. A loss means water left, so the solution was more concentrated. No change means the two had the same concentration. Keep the size of the tissue, the volume of solution, the time and the temperature the same, so that only the concentration changes.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks why small cells exchange substances faster than large ones
variantes.contenu_markdown: For a cube of side $a$ cm, surface area $= 6a^2$ and volume $= a^3$. For $a = 1$ the ratio of surface area to volume is 6; for $a = 2$ it is 3. As an organism or cell gets larger, its surface area to volume ratio falls, so diffusion alone can no longer supply the centre quickly enough. This is why large organisms need transport systems and why exchange surfaces such as the lungs and root hairs have a large surface area.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question describes a situation and asks which process is involved
variantes.contenu_markdown: Ask two questions. First: is energy from respiration needed? If yes, it is active transport. If no, ask: is it only water crossing a membrane from a dilute to a concentrated side? If yes, it is osmosis; otherwise it is diffusion. A clue for active transport is a substance moving into a cell that already holds more of it than the surroundings, or a supply of oxygen being needed for the process.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Four identical cylinders, each of mass 5.0 g, were cut from a yam. One was placed in distilled water, and the others in sugar solutions A and B, each for 40 minutes. After blotting dry, the masses were 5.6 g (distilled water), 5.0 g (solution A) and 4.3 g (solution B).

(a) Calculate the percentage change in mass in each liquid.
(b) Which solution had the same concentration as the cell sap of the yam? Give a reason.
(c) Explain, using osmosis, the mass of the cylinder in solution B.

etapes.action: Write the formula for percentage change.
etapes.justification: The same formula must be used for every cylinder so that results can be compared.

etapes.resultat_markdown: Distilled water: $\dfrac{5.6 - 5.0}{5.0} \times 100 = +12\%$. Solution A: $\dfrac{5.0 - 5.0}{5.0} \times 100 = 0\%$. Solution B: $\dfrac{4.3 - 5.0}{5.0} \times 100 = -14\%$.

etapes.action: Identify the solution with no change in mass.
etapes.justification: No net movement of water means that the concentration outside equals the concentration of the cell sap.

etapes.action: Explain the loss in solution B.
etapes.justification: Water moves from a dilute solution to a more concentrated one through the selectively permeable membrane of the cells.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Solution B was more concentrated than the cell sap, so water left the yam cells by osmosis and the cylinder lost mass.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) Distilled water $+12\%$, solution A $0\%$, solution B $-14\%$. (b) Solution A, because the mass did not change, so there was no net movement of water. (c) Solution B was more concentrated than the cell sap, so water left the cells by osmosis and the mass fell.

items.erreur_markdown: Osmosis is the movement of any molecules from a high to a low concentration through a membrane.
items.pourquoi_faux: Osmosis involves water only. Other molecules moving down a concentration gradient are diffusing.
items.correction_markdown: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules from a dilute solution to a more concentrated one through a selectively permeable membrane.

items.erreur_markdown: Active transport moves substances from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration using energy.
items.pourquoi_faux: The direction is wrong. Moving from high to low concentration is diffusion, which is passive. Active transport goes against the gradient, from low to high.
items.correction_markdown: Active transport: low to high concentration, against the gradient, using energy from respiration.

items.erreur_markdown: A plant cell placed in pure water becomes plasmolysed.
items.pourquoi_faux: In pure water a plant cell takes in water by osmosis and becomes turgid. The cell wall stops it from bursting. Plasmolysis occurs in a concentrated solution.
items.correction_markdown: Pure water: turgid cell. Concentrated solution: plasmolysed cell.

items.erreur_markdown: Water moves from the concentrated solution to the dilute solution.
items.pourquoi_faux: This reverses the direction. Water moves towards the more concentrated solution, from the dilute side.
items.correction_markdown: Water moves from the dilute solution to the more concentrated solution.

items.enonce_markdown:
Name the process (diffusion, osmosis or active transport) in each case.

(a) The smell of roasting fish spreads through the air.
(b) Root hair cells absorb nitrate ions from soil water that contains fewer nitrate ions than the cells.
(c) Water enters a root hair cell from the wet soil.
(d) Carbon dioxide leaves the blood and enters the air sacs of the lungs.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Diffusion**, because the smell molecules spread from high to low concentration.
(b) **Active transport**, because the ions move against the gradient and the cells use energy.
(c) **Osmosis**, because only water moves, from a dilute solution (soil water) to a more concentrated one (cell sap).
(d) **Diffusion**, from a high to a low concentration of carbon dioxide.

items.enonce_markdown:
Two strips of carrot, each of mass 8.0 g, were left for one hour, one in solution X and the other in solution Y. Their masses were then 8.8 g (in X) and 7.2 g (in Y).

(a) Calculate the percentage change in mass for each strip.
(b) State which solution was more concentrated than the cell sap and explain your answer.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) X: $\dfrac{8.8 - 8.0}{8.0} \times 100 =$ **+10%**. Y: $\dfrac{7.2 - 8.0}{8.0} \times 100 =$ **$-10\%$**.
(b) **Solution Y** was more concentrated than the cell sap. The strip lost mass because water left the cells by osmosis, moving towards the more concentrated solution. In X the strip gained mass because X was more dilute than the cell sap, so water entered the cells.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Cube P has sides of 2 cm and cube Q has sides of 4 cm. Calculate the surface area to volume ratio of each, and say which cube would take up a dissolved substance into its centre faster by diffusion.
(b) A farmer put a large amount of fertiliser close to young maize plants and the leaves soon wilted. Explain why.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Cube P: surface area $= 6 \times 2^2 = 24$ cm², volume $= 2^3 = 8$ cm³, ratio $=$ **3**. Cube Q: surface area $= 6 \times 4^2 = 96$ cm², volume $= 4^3 = 64$ cm³, ratio $=$ **1.5**. Cube P has the larger ratio and the shorter distance to the centre, so it takes up the substance faster.
(b) The fertiliser made the soil water very concentrated, more concentrated than the cell sap of the root hair cells. Water therefore left the root cells by osmosis. The cells lost turgor, the plant could not be supported and the leaves wilted.

items_markdown: Diffusion: net movement from high to low concentration, passive, no energy needed.
Osmosis: movement of water only, from a dilute to a more concentrated solution, through a selectively permeable membrane.
Active transport: movement from low to high concentration, against the gradient, using energy from respiration and carrier proteins.
Plant cells become turgid in dilute solutions and plasmolysed in concentrated ones; animal cells may burst or shrink.
Percentage change in mass $= \dfrac{\text{final} - \text{initial}}{\text{initial}} \times 100$; a gain means the outside solution was more dilute than the cell sap.
